+"""Directed residual transport in the nearest-codeword frame."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def mechanism_loss(source, target, codebook, mask, **parameters):
+    """Compute the proposal's masked transport and separation-barrier loss.
+
+    Nearest-neighbour indices are discrete; selected codebook vectors remain in
+    the graph so gradients reach both endpoint codewords.
+    """
+    alpha = float(parameters.get("alpha", 0.5))
+    lambda_transport = float(parameters.get("lambda_transport", 0.01))
+    lambda_sep = float(parameters.get("lambda_sep", 0.01))
+    margin = float(parameters.get("margin", 0.25))
+
+    source_idx = torch.cdist(source, codebook).argmin(dim=1)
+    target_idx = torch.cdist(target, codebook).argmin(dim=1)
+    source_code = codebook[source_idx]
+    target_code = codebook[target_idx]
+
+    # Directed frame: source residual is transported toward the target using
+    # target-code minus source-code displacement (not an unordered pair loss).
+    displacement = target_code - source_code
+    source_residual = source - source_code
+    target_residual = target - target_code
+    error = target_residual - (source_residual + alpha * displacement)
+
+    valid = mask.to(dtype=source.dtype, device=source.device).reshape(-1)
+    denom = valid.sum().clamp_min(1.0)
+    transport = (error.square().sum(dim=-1) * valid).sum() / denom
+    distance = torch.linalg.vector_norm(displacement, dim=-1)
+    separation = (torch.relu(margin - distance).square() * valid).sum() / denom
+    return lambda_transport * transport + lambda_sep * separation
